selectedQuotations.englishQuote: In truth, the blessed God cannot be grasped at all, and the description ‘holy’ does not apply to Him except because Israel recognizes His holiness. This is what is called apprehending Him: that He is holy, separate from every apprehension. Through this, the blessed God is called holy. This is why, concerning God’s holiness, he brought the verse, ‘You are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Israel’: through Israel’s praises, the blessed God is called holy, because they recognize His holiness and kingship.

selectedQuotations.hebrewQuote: הקב"ה מלא כל הארץ כבודו ולית אתר פנוי מיני' רק שהוא בהעלם גדול וישת חושך סתרו. וכאשר מאיר ללב האדם הכרה זו איך השי"ת מלא כל הארץ כבודו זה נקרא הוציאנו מאפלה לאור גדול כמ"ש בהגדה. דיציאת מצרים שהוא הוצאה מן ההעלם הכרת הש"י אל הגילוי. והוא הארה לגבי האדם וגם לגבי הש"י כמשאז"ל (ב"ר סוף פר' ל) משל למלך שהי' מהלך במבואות אפלות ובא אוהבו והדליק את הנר. שאברהם אבינו ע"ה האיר לפני הש"י כי זה נקרא שכינה בגלות כאשר שכינתו ית' בתחתונים הוא בהעלם עצום ואינו בהתגלות ובפרסום הרי זה כמהלך במבואות אפלות.
selectedQuotations.englishQuote: The Holy One, blessed be He—His glory fills the whole earth, and no place is empty of Him. Yet He is greatly concealed: ‘He makes darkness His hiding place.’ When this recognition illuminates a person’s heart—how the blessed God’s glory fills the whole earth—this is called ‘He brought us from darkness to great light,’ as stated in the Haggadah. The Exodus from Egypt is the passage from the concealment of the recognition of the blessed God into its revelation. It is an illumination both for the person and for the blessed God, as our Sages said at the end of Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 30: a parable of a king walking through dark alleyways, whose friend came and lit a lamp. Abraham our father, peace be upon him, illuminated before the blessed God. For this is called the Divine Presence in exile: when His Presence among the lower beings is profoundly concealed and is neither revealed nor publicly known, it is like walking through dark alleyways.

selectedQuotations.englishQuote: He said this concerning the tribe of Asher in accordance with what I heard from our holy master, of blessed memory. He said that Amos, who was of the tribe of Asher and came from Tekoa, spoke the passage ‘Are you not like the children of Cush?’ It is founded upon the cry of young people, for one who has blemished the covenant is called disfigured and Cushite—the opposite of Joseph, who is called ‘handsome in form and handsome in appearance.’ This is because that blemish is more common in this tribe. Thus far his words. The meaning is that this tribe was given an especially great power to repair the serpent’s blemish and corruption. Its root was in eating; subsequently it extended to his coming upon Eve and imparting impurity to her, from which the corruption of the hundred and thirty years extended.

selectedQuotations.englishQuote: Afterward the holy Zohar says: ‘Great is crying out, for it rules in this world and the World to Come; through crying out a person inherits this world and the World to Come,’ as it is written, ‘They cried out to the Lord,’ and so forth. Its proof is that the passage begins, ‘Let the redeemed of the Lord say so.’ This refers to the World to Come: Binah, the world that is coming. For when a person takes to heart that the supreme King of kings stands over him, awe reaches him. This is ‘The beginning of wisdom is fear of the Lord’; the Shabbat of Friday evening ‘is awe, and awe rests within it’ (Zohar I, 5b). The lower Divine Presence is also called the heart, as ‘but he has no heart’ is interpreted in Yoma 72b concerning one who lacks fear of Heaven. Through awe one comes to repentance: the expression ‘awe’ is interpreted as repentance in Avodah Zarah 19a and Berakhot 17a, for through awe a person remembers his sins, regrets them and repents of them. When awe enters the depths of the heart, ‘His heart will understand, and he will return’—this is Binah, the heart. Thus, ‘it rules in this world’ means awe, which is the attribute of Malchut; ‘and in the World to Come’ means repentance, Binah, the world that is coming.

selectedQuotations.englishQuote: The Holy One, blessed be He, who is called righteous and upright, created the human being in His image only so that he would be righteous and upright like Him. If you ask, ‘Why did He create the evil inclination, of which it is written, “The inclination of the human heart is evil from youth” (Genesis 8:21)? You say that it is evil—who can make it good?’ the Holy One, blessed be He, says: ‘You make it evil.’ Why? A child of five, six, seven, eight or nine does not sin; rather, from ten onward, he then develops the evil inclination.

Moses transmitted them to Israel as laws without their reasons. No person can arrive at their reasons through prophecy except Moses, of whom it is written, ‘No prophet has arisen again,’ and so forth. selectedQuotations.englishQuote: In the Rav’s Siddur, on the verse “From new moon to its new moon,” he asks why it says “its new moon.” We may say that a month is named for renewal. Thus “its new moon” hints that each Rosh Chodesh has a different renewal: each of the twelve months of the year has its own arrangement of the letters of the divine Name, its own one of the twelve simple letters, and its own bodily organ, as stated in Sefer Yetzirah. Likewise, in every year each Rosh Chodesh has a new renewal. “From Sabbath to its Sabbath” also hints at this: each Sabbath has a fresh renewal of holiness. Hence it is called a bride each and every Sabbath. A woman is a bride only once, during the seven days of celebration; but every Sabbath has a different, newly shining holiness.

selectedQuotations.englishQuote: There is an evil inclination of desire that is called fire. Likewise, the inclination of jealousy and honor is also called fire, as explained in Vayera, teaching 1, beginning “And also.” There is also the shell of Amalek, of whom it says, “who cooled you”—who chilled and cooled you. This means that he casts coldness and laziness upon a person. This is the first of the shells, and it assails even great people. Thus concerning Jabez they interpreted “that it not cause me pain” (Temurah 16a): “that the evil inclination not prevent me from studying.” The root of the serpent and the evil inclination is called sadness, for it brought sadness and toil into the world. This is “She does not fear snow for her household.” Not only does she not fear the fire of desire, jealousy, and honor—the three kinds of fire—but she does not even fear snow, the first of the shells, which casts laziness and coldness. “She does not fear for her household” means the great people who are called her household. Why? “For all her household are clothed in two”—Sabbath and circumcision, both of which indicate that they are attached at the root to the utterance “In the beginning,” the beginning of holiness.

selectedQuotations.englishQuote: If it says, “I shall be with your mouth,” why does it say, “I shall instruct you”? And if it says, “I shall instruct you,” why does it say, “I shall be with your mouth”? Rather, this teaches that “I shall be with your mouth” refers to the opening of the mouth and the tongue’s response. “I shall instruct you” refers to the treasures of wisdom that the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed to him, so that through his wisdom he could see all the orders of creation, as it is said, “Not so My servant Moses: in all My house he is faithful” (Shelach). It does not say “in My house,” but “in all My house.” This teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, placed Moses in charge of all Israel and all the treasures of Torah, all the treasures of wisdom, all the treasures of understanding, all the treasures of discernment, all the treasures of knowledge, the treasures of the Garden of Eden, and all the treasures of life. He showed him all the precious things of this world and all the precious things of the World to Come.

In his old age he taught, “Gold acquires silver”: the ultimate clarification that awe belongs to holiness comes precisely when manifest joy arises from it—“my joy came from my awe.” The soul is then perfected in complete holiness, when the holiness corresponding to the three holy patriarchs is completed within it.

selectedQuotations.hebrewQuote: ומזה יהי' נכון לבנו בטוח בה' שגם תפלותינו אינם חוזרים ריקם שאנו מתפללים תמיד ולירושלים עירך ברחמים תשוב הגם שאין אנו זוכים עוד בפועל אל יפול לב האדם עליו. מפני שבאמת כל התפלות של נפשות ישראל פועלים ברוחניות כל פרט נפש לפי ערך תשוקתו כך הוא זוכה לתכלית המכוון להתנחם בלבו כמו שא' ז"ל כל המתאבל על ירושלים זוכה ורואה בשמחתה. וזה בודאי אין המכוון לעתיד לבא כי הלא נאמר בלשון הווה זוכה ורואה וכו' רק שלפי ערך התשוקה והגעגועים שלו בפנימיות הלב לעומת כן הוא זוכה מיד להיות רואה ומרגיש בלבו בשמחתה בבחי' שמחו צדיקים בה'. ועבור זה נתקנו כל נוסח התפלות בלשון הווה בונה ירושלים מצמיח קרן ישועה המחזיר שכינתו לציון מפני שבאמת המה נענים בתמידיות וכמו שנא' ישמח ישראל בעושיו בני ציון יגילו במלכם:
selectedQuotations.englishQuote: From this our hearts should become steadfast in trust in God: our prayers, too, do not return empty. We continually pray, “Return to Jerusalem, Your city, in mercy.” Even though we have not yet merited this in actuality, a person’s heart must not fail him. In truth, all the prayers of Israel’s souls act spiritually. Each individual soul, according to the measure of its longing, attains the intended purpose and finds consolation in its heart, as the Sages said: “Whoever mourns for Jerusalem merits and sees its joy.” This certainly does not mean only the future, for it says in the present tense, “merits and sees.” Rather, according to the measure of the longing and yearning in the depths of his heart, he immediately merits to see and feel its joy in his heart, in the sense of “Rejoice in God, you righteous.” For this reason all the formulas of prayer were established in the present tense: “Who builds Jerusalem,” “Who causes the horn of salvation to spring forth,” and “Who restores His Presence to Zion.” In truth, they are continually answered, as it says: “Let Israel rejoice in its Maker; let the children of Zion exult in their King.”
selectedQuotations.connectionRationaleForAuditOnly: Expands the precise claim that the individual worshipper is answered now even before the collective restoration; provides the explanation for present-tense prayer formulations.

selectedQuotations.anchorHebrew: נִצְרָךְ הִתְרַבּוּת שֶׁל רֹב חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, מַה שֶּׁאָדָם מַמְצִיא מִנַּפְשׁוֹ.
selectedQuotations.hebrewQuote: ושמעתי מאדומו"ר זצל"ה שאמר מהאי טעמא אמרו בגמ' בכמה מקומות אליבי' דהאי כי הד"ת שבע"פ הם יוצאים מקירות לבו של האדם כפי הרגשתו הקדושה בלבו וכדכתיב כי ברוב חכמה רוב כעס היינו שע"י הרוב חכמה התושבע"פ מתיישר הלב מהרוב כעס ומתקן את הרוב הכעס.
selectedQuotations.englishQuote: I heard from my master, of blessed memory, that for this reason the Talmud says in many places, “According to the heart of this one”: the words of Oral Torah issue from the depths of a person’s heart, according to the holy feeling within his heart. As it is written, “With much wisdom comes much vexation”: through the great wisdom of Oral Torah, the heart is straightened out from its great vexation, and that great vexation is repaired.
selectedQuotations.connectionRationaleForAuditOnly: A reported teaching directly joins personal heart-born Torah with repair of the vexation of the foolish heart. The teacher is unnamed in the quoted passage; no unverified personal attribution is added.

selectedQuotations.hebrewQuote: וכתיב כי תבא חכמה ללבך ודעת לנפשך ינעם שכשיכנס החכמה ללב יזכה אחר כך להדעת ופירש לנפשך ינעם שירגיש טעם בדברי תורה ונועם הוא בינה כמ"ש בזוהר הקדוש (ח"ב ל"א ב') וזה שנאמר כי נעים וגו' היינו דכתיב ובדעת חדרים ימלאו כל הון יקר ונעים. דעת היינו כשנכנס היראה למעמקי הלב וכמו שנאמר אז תבין יראת ה' ודעת אלהים תמצא. וזה שא' חדרים ימלאו כל הון יקר ונעים שהוא בחינת בינה היינו שירגיש טעם ונועם בדברי תורה וזה הפירוש כי נעים.
selectedQuotations.englishQuote: It is written, “When wisdom enters your heart, and knowledge is pleasant to your soul”: when wisdom enters the heart, one afterward attains knowledge. “Pleasant to your soul” means that one feels a taste in the words of Torah. Pleasantness is understanding, as stated in the holy Zohar (II 31b). This is the meaning of “For they are pleasant,” as it is written, “Through knowledge, chambers are filled with every precious and pleasant treasure.” Knowledge means that awe enters the depths of the heart, as it is written, “Then you will understand the fear of God and find the knowledge of God.” This is “chambers are filled with every precious and pleasant treasure”: the aspect of understanding, meaning that one feels taste and pleasantness in the words of Torah. This is the meaning of “For they are pleasant.”
selectedQuotations.connectionRationaleForAuditOnly: Clarifies the text’s “pleasantness” and “sweeter than honey” through Rav Tzadok’s own definition of Torah taste as wisdom reaching the depths of the heart.

selectedQuotations.hebrewQuote: אמר להם הקדוש ברוך הוא לא שאני צריך לכם, אלא שתאירו לי כדרך שהארתי לכם, למה, לעלות אתכם בפני האמות, שיהיו אומרים ראו היאך ישראל מאירין למי שהוא מאיר לכל העולם. משל למה הדבר דומה לפקח וסומא שהיו מהלכין בדרך, אמר לו פקח לסומא כשנכנס לתוך הבית צא והדלק לי את הנר הזה והאר לי, אמר לו הסומא בטובתך כשהייתי בדרך אתה היית מסמכני עד שנכנסנו לתוך הבית אתה היית מלוה אותי, ועכשו אתה אומר הדלק לי את הנר הזה והאר לי. אמר לו הפקח שלא תהא מחזיק לי טובה שהייתי מלוך בדרך, לכך אמרתי לך האר לי.
selectedQuotations.englishQuote: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: “It is not that I need you, but that you should give Me light as I gave you light.” Why? To raise your standing before the nations, so that they will say, “See how Israel gives light to the One who gives light to the entire world.” To what may this be compared? To a sighted person and a blind person who were walking on the road. When they entered the house, the sighted person said to the blind person, “Go and light this lamp for me, and give me light.” The blind person said to him, “Please! When I was on the road you supported me; until we entered the house you accompanied me. Now you tell me, ‘Light this lamp for me and give me light’?” The sighted person said to him, “So that you should not feel indebted to me for having accompanied you on the road, I therefore told you: Give me light.”
selectedQuotations.connectionRationaleForAuditOnly: Corrects a plainly unrelated inherited quotation about Moses struggling with the Menorah. This is the exact parable cited by the main text.

paragraphs.text: Bamidbar Rabbah 15:4: “Another reading: "When you raise up". You see that Moshe struggled [nitkasha] with the design of the Menorah more than all the other vessels of the Mishkan [Tabernacle], until the Holy One Who is Blessed showed him with a finger. Similarly with the hoofs of impure and pure animals, as it says, "These are the animals which you shall eat" (Vayikra 11:4), these are the ones which you shall not eat, and showed him with a finger. Similarly with the moon, "this month is for you" (Shmot 12:2). Similarly with the Menorah, "This is how the Menorah was made: it was hammered work [miksha] of gold" (Bemidbar 8:4), which is to say how hard [kasha] it is to make, since Moshe became weary on account of it. When he struggled, The Holy One Who is Blessed said to Moshe: take a talent of gold and throw it in the fire and take it out, and it will be formed on its own, as it says, "its cups, calyxes, and petals were of one piece with it [lit: came out from it]" (Shmot 37:17) - he would strike it with a hammer and it would be made on its own. Therefore it says "it will be made [te'aseh] of hammered work" (Shmot 25:31) written with a [Hebrew letter] "yod" and not written "you will make [ta'aseh]", that is to say it will be made on its own. Moshe took the talent [of gold] and threw it in the fire. Moshe said, "Master of the Universe, behold the talent is in the fire. Whatever you wish - so shall it be done." The Menorah immediately came out made according to its design, thus it is written, "According to the pattern that the LORD had shown Moses..." (Bemidbar 8:4). It is not written here "so did Moses make the Menorah," rather "so was the Menorah made." And who made it? The Holy One Who is Blessed. Therefore the Holy One Who is Blessed said to Moshe: If you are careful to light [it] before me, I will protect your souls from every evil thing, since souls are compared to a candle, as it says. "the candle of Adonai is the soul of a person" (Proverbs 20:27) and it says, "When you raise up the candles)" (Bemidbar 8:2)”

selectedQuotations.hebrewQuote: אמר רבי שמעון אב לא למדו, ורב לא היה לו, ומהיכן למד את התורה, אלא זמן לו הקדוש ברוך הוא שתי כליותיו כמין שני רבנים, והיו נובעות ומלמדות אותו תורה וחכמה, הדא הוא דכתיב (תהלים טז, ז): אברך את ה' אשר יעצני אף לילות יסרוני כליותי.
selectedQuotations.englishQuote: Rabbi Shimon said: His father did not teach him, and he had no teacher. From where, then, did he learn Torah? The Holy One, blessed be He, appointed his two kidneys as two teachers, and they welled forth and taught him Torah and wisdom. Thus it is written: “I bless God, who counseled me; even at night my kidneys instruct me” (Psalms 16:7).

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 61:7: ““But to the sons of the concubines that Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts; and he sent them away from Isaac his son, during his lifetime, eastward, to the east country” (Genesis 25:6). “But to the sons of the concubines…” – In the days of Alexander of Macedonia, the children of Ishmael came to lodge a claim against Israel regarding the birthright. Two evil families, the Canaanites and the Egyptians, came with them. They [the rabbis] said: ‘Who will go and contend with them?’ Gevia ben Kosem said: ‘I will go and contend with them.’ They told him: ‘Be careful that you do not cede the Land to them.’ He said: ‘I am going to contend with them; if I am victorious, it is well and good, and if not, you can always say: Who is this lowly person, that he should represent us?’ He went and contended with them. Alexander of Macedonia said to them: ‘Who is lodging a claim against whom?’ The Ishmaelites said: ‘We are lodging a claim against them [Israel], and it is on the basis of their own Torah that we come against them. It is written: “Rather, he shall acknowledge the firstborn, son of the hated wife [to give him a double portion]” (Deuteronomy 21:17). By right, Ishmael is entitled to receive a double portion.’ Gevia ben Kosem said to him: ‘My lord the king, may a person not do as he pleases for his owns sons?’ He said to him: ‘Yes.’ He said to him: ‘Is it not written: “Abraham gave all that was his to Isaac”?’ (Genesis 25:5). They said to him: ‘Where is the document of gifts that he divided among his sons?’ He said to them: “And to the sons of the concubines of Abraham, Abraham gave gifts.” They departed from there shamefacedly. The Canaanites said: ‘It is on the basis of their own Torah that we come against them. It is written everywhere: “To the land of Canaan,” “the land of Canaan” – let them give us back our land.’ Gevia ben Kosem said to them: ‘My lord the king, may a person not do as he pleases with his slave?’ He said to him: ‘Yes.’ He said to him: ‘What is written? “Cursed is Canaan, a slave of slaves…. [And he said: Blessed be the Lord, God of Shem, and Canaan shall be slaves unto them]” (Genesis 9:25–26). The Land is ours and they are slaves to my lord the king.’ They departed from there shamefacedly. The Egyptians said: ‘It is on the basis of their own Torah that we come against them. Six hundred thousand [Israelite] men departed from our midst laden with silver vessels and gold vessels, as it is written: “They stripped Egypt” (Exodus 12:36). Let them give us back our silver and our gold.’ Gevia ben Kosem said to him: ‘My lord the king, six hundred thousand people spent two hundred and ten years in their midst, among them silversmiths and among them goldsmiths, who normally receive one dinar a day as wages. The philosophers sat and calculated and did not even reach one hundred years [of labor] before the land of Egypt would be found to be bankrupt.’ They departed from there shamefacedly. He [Alexander] once sought to ascend to Jerusalem. The Samaritans went and said to him: ‘Be aware that they will not allow you to enter their Holy of Holies.’ When Gevia ben Kosem sensed this, he went and made two felt shoes for him and placed on them two gems, each valued at twenty thousand silver dinars. When he [Alexander] reached the Temple Mount, he [Gevia] said to him: ‘My lord the king, remove your shoes and put on these felt shoes, the floor being slippery, so your feet should not slip.’ When he reached the Holy of Holies, they said to him: ‘Until here we have permission to enter; from here on, we do not have permission to enter.’ He said to him [Gevia]: ‘When I leave here, I will flatten your forehead’ [variant reading: Your hump]. He said to him: ‘If you can do that, you would be an expert doctor, and could charge a great fee.’ “And sent them away from Isaac his son [eastward, to the east country]” – he said to them: As far east as you can go, go east, so you will not be burned by Isaac’s coals. But Esau, because he came to confront Jacob, he received his punishment from him. That is what is written: “Is it for you to be jovial, like those in antiquity whose legs led them afar to live? Who devised this against Tyre [Tzor] the glorious…” (Isaiah 23:7–8). Rabbi Elazar said: Every instance of Tzor that is written in the Bible with a vav, the verse is speaking of the city of Tyre; when it is without a vav, the verse is speaking of Rome. “The glorious [ma’atira]” – Rabbi Abba said: It was surrounded [with riches] like a crown [atara]. Rabbi Yanai said in the name of Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Yanai: It was surrounded by thorns.”

When he [Alexander] reached the Temple Mount, he [Gevia] said to him: ‘My lord the king, remove your shoes and put on these felt shoes, the floor being slippery, so your feet should not slip.’ When he reached the Holy of Holies, they said to him: ‘Until here we have permission to enter; from here on, we do not have permission to enter.’ He said to him [Gevia]: ‘When I leave here, I will flatten your forehead’ [variant reading: Your hump]. He said to him: ‘If you can do that, you would be an expert doctor, and could charge a great fee.’ “And sent them away from Isaac his son [eastward, to the east country]” – he said to them: As far east as you can go, go east, so you will not be burned by Isaac’s coals. But Esau, because he came to confront Jacob, he received his punishment from him. That is what is written: “Is it for you to be jovial, like those in antiquity whose legs led them afar to live? Who devised this against Tyre [Tzor] the glorious…” (Isaiah 23:7–8). Rabbi Elazar said: Every instance of Tzor that is written in the Bible with a vav, the verse is speaking of the city of Tyre; when it is without a vav, the verse is speaking of Rome. “The glorious [ma’atira]” – Rabbi Abba said: It was surrounded [with riches] like a crown [atara]. Rabbi Yanai said in the name of Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Yanai: It was surrounded by thorns.”

selectedQuotations.hebrewQuote: את מוצא למעלה אחד עשר שבטים הקריבו ושבט אפרים הקריב, וכל הנשיאים הקריבו חוץ מנשיאו של לוי, ומי היה נשיאו של לוי, זה אהרן, שנאמר (במדבר יז, יח): ואת שם אהרן תכתב על מטה לוי, ואהרן לא הקריב עם הנשיאים, והיה אומר אוי לי שמא בשבילי אין הקדוש ברוך הוא מקבל שבטו של לוי, אמר לו הקדוש ברוך הוא למשה לך אמר לו לאהרן אל תתירא לגדולה מזו אתה מתקן. לכך נאמר: דבר אל אהרן ואמרת אליו בהעלתך את הנרת. הקרבנות, כל זמן שבית המקדש קים הם נוהגים, אבל הנרות לעולם (במדבר ח, ב): אל מול פני המנורה יאירו, וכל הברכות שנתתי לך לברך את בני, אינן בטלין לעולם.
selectedQuotations.englishQuote: You find above that eleven tribes brought offerings, and the tribe of Ephraim brought an offering; all the princes brought offerings except the prince of Levi. Who was the prince of Levi? Aharon, as it says: “Write Aharon’s name upon the staff of Levi.” Aharon had not brought an offering with the princes, and he said: Woe to me! Perhaps it is because of me that the Holy One, blessed be He, does not accept the tribe of Levi. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moshe: Go and tell Aharon: Do not fear; you are destined for something greater than this. Therefore it says: “Speak to Aharon and say to him: When you kindle the lamps.” The sacrifices apply as long as the Temple stands, but the lamps are forever: “They shall shine toward the face of the menorah.” All the blessings I gave you with which to bless My children will likewise never cease.
selectedQuotations.repairReason: Restore the correct Bamidbar Rabbah 15:6 quotation already present in the print master; the reader wrongly repeats a paraphrase of 15:5.
selectedQuotations.oldText: Bamidbar Rabbah 15:6: “The Midrash Rabba (Bamidbar 15:5) relates that when the Jews were given the commandment to kindle the Menorah in the Temple (Bamidbar 8:2), they asked G'd why He told them to light up for Him Who is the Light of the whole world. G'd said to them, "You are right. I do not need your light. But I want to give you an opportunity to light for Me like I have lit for you." G'd led the Jewish people with a cloud of glory and a pillar of fire. This is why He told them to kindle the lights when the Tabernacle was erected. "This will elevate your position amongst the nations. They should say, look how the Jewish nation lights for the One who lights up the whole world." [...] The Midrash explains that this can be compared to a seeing person who leads a blind person as they travel along the road together. When they come to the house, the seeing person says to the blind one, "Please go and light a candle for me." To this the blind person replies, "I do not understand. As long as we were travelling, you supported and guided me. Why do you now ask me to light a candle for you?" To this the seeing person responds, "I want to give you an opportunity to pay me back so that you do not feel an ongoing debt of gratitude".”

selectedQuotations.anchorHebrew: וְהָרַמְבַּ"ן (פָּרָשַׁת וַיְחִי) כָּתַב שֶׁמִּפְּנֵי זֶה נֶעֶנְשׁוּ הַחַשְׁמוֹנָאִים
selectedQuotations.hebrewQuote: וזה היה ענש החשמונאים, שמלכו בבית שני, כי היו חסידי עליון, ואלמלא הם נשתכחו התורה והמצות מישראל, ואף על פי כן נענשו ענש גדול, כי ארבעת בני חשמונאי הזקן החסידים המולכים זה אחר זה, עם כל גבורתם והצלחתם, נפלו ביד אויביהם בחרב, והגיע הענש בסוף למה שאמרו רז"ל (בבא בתרא ג א): "כל מאן דאמר מבית חשמונאי קאתינא עבדא הוא", שנכרתו כלם בעון הזה. ואף על פי שהיה בזרע שמעון ענש מן הצדוקים, אבל כל זרע מתתיה חשמונאי הצדיק לא אבדו אלא בעבור זה שמלכו ולא היו מזרע יהודה ומבית דוד, והסירו השבט והמחוקק לגמרי, והיה עונשם מדה כנגד מדה, שהמשיל הקדוש ברוך הוא עליהם את עבדיהם והם הכריתום.
selectedQuotations.englishQuote: This was the punishment of the Hasmoneans who reigned during the Second Temple. They were supremely pious, and without them the Torah and the commandments would have been forgotten in Israel. Nevertheless, they were severely punished: the four pious sons of the elder Hasmonean who reigned one after another, despite all their strength and success, fell by the sword into the hands of their enemies. The punishment ultimately reached the point described by our Sages: “Anyone who says, ‘I descend from the house of the Hasmoneans,’ is a slave,” for they were all cut off because of this sin. Although the descendants of Shimon suffered punishment because of the Sadducees, all the descendants of the righteous Matityahu the Hasmonean perished only because they reigned without belonging to the tribe of Judah or the house of David, completely removing the scepter and the ruler’s staff. Their punishment was measure for measure: the Holy One, blessed be He, gave their slaves power over them, and they destroyed them.
selectedQuotations.repairReason: Replace modern summary with Ramban’s actual argument, retaining his praise of the Hasmoneans, the precise accusation, and the stated punishment.
selectedQuotations.oldText: Ramban on Genesis 49:10: ‘The scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor the ruler’s staff from between his feet’ (Genesis 49:10): Ramban explains that Jacob vested kingship exclusively in the tribe of Judah and the house of David. Therefore, although the Hasmoneans were saintly priests who saved Israel and restored the Torah and Temple service, they were severely punished and their dynasty fell because they assumed the royal crown (malchut) for themselves instead of reserving kingship for Judah.’

selectedQuotations.englishQuote: “And His Holy One into a flame”—this is Esther. This follows the statement in Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 21, that the Holy One, blessed be He, covered Esther with His sign, for she is His holiness. That is, Esther too was of the aspect of Joseph the righteous. As stated at the beginning of Midrash Rabbah on Kedoshim, wherever you find a boundary against sexual immorality, you find holiness: anyone who guards himself against sexual immorality is called holy. Thus the Gemara, Megillah 13a, says: Her name was Esther; why was she called Hadassah? After the righteous, who are called myrtles. The righteous are called myrtles because a myrtle gives a pleasant fragrance. Eruvin 21b states: “The mandrakes gave forth fragrance”—these are the young men of Israel who have not tasted sin. We have often explained that the expression “young men of Israel” appears to refer to the sin of damaging the covenant, to which youth gives rise, as explained concerning Rosh Chodesh Marcheshvan. A righteous person who is a vehicle for the quality “foundation of the world” is called a myrtle because he gives a pleasant fragrance. Since Esther was called Hadassah, it follows that she was righteous and holy, of the aspect of Joseph the righteous.

selectedQuotations.englishQuote: As we have already said, a person is called one who journeys throughout his life, as it is said, “For the person journeys to his eternal home.” Every righteous person has a world of his own, as Midrash Rabbah, Pekudei 52, says: It does not say “worlds,” but “his world.” All the working days correspond to “When the Ark journeyed … may Your enemies scatter and those who hate You flee.” Then a person journeys from stage to stage. When Shabbat comes, it is “When it rested, he would say: Return, O Lord.” The holiness of Shabbat always accords with the holiness of the labor of the working days; thus the six working days are always mentioned before Shabbat, as explained in Kedushat Shabbat 1 and elsewhere. On Shabbat, holiness then shines into the working days that follow, and they possess greater holiness than the preceding six working days. When the second Shabbat arrives, it gains further holiness; it likewise bestows greater holiness on the coming working days. So it continues forever: throughout his life, the person journeys.

selectedQuotations.englishQuote: We find in the Talmud, Bava Batra 172a and elsewhere, the case of two people living in one town, each named Joseph son of Simeon. It would seemingly have been more fitting to use the example Reuben son of Jacob; why specifically Joseph son of Simeon? We have explained that all Israel are called by Joseph’s name, as it is said, “The remnant of Joseph,” and as stated in Bereshit Rabbah 71. This accords with “Your people are all righteous,” and with the statement of the holy Zohar, II, 23a: everyone who is circumcised is called righteous. Thus it uses Joseph son of Simeon as its example. Even though most of the twenty-four thousand who died over the matter of Peor were from the tribe of Simeon, which is the opposite of the quality of Joseph the righteous, in truth he too is called by Joseph’s name: the quality of the righteous person who guards the covenant. This is the meaning of Joseph son of Simeon.

selectedQuotations.englishQuote: At the beginning of creation, the essence of life was words of Torah. Even eating, which sustains life, was also words of Torah, as it is said, “Come, eat of My bread and drink of the wine I have mixed,” interpreted in the holy Zohar, III, 271b, as the bread of the Written Torah and the wine of the Oral Torah. After the corruption that came through eating, when good and evil became mixed, nevertheless, when the festival of Rosh Hashanah arrives—the day of the world’s conception—one can also merit to taste only the good, as will be in the future. As I heard from our holy master of Ishbitz, of blessed memory, who said that in the future the verse will be joined as follows: “From every tree of the garden you may eat, and from the Tree of Knowledge of good”—you may also eat; “and evil you shall not eat.” Only the evil of the Tree of Knowledge shall you not eat. It will then become clear that Israel never ate anything but the good of the Tree of Knowledge. That is, the intention was solely words of Torah—Torah is light—and it is written, “God saw the light, that it was good.”

selectedQuotations.englishQuote: This is the meaning of “You shall draw water with joy”: water means Torah, and it is the Oral Torah that is compared to water. paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 72a:4: “The Gemara relates: There was a certain man who said to the Sages: I am from a place called Shot Mishot. Rabbi Yitzḥak Nappaḥa stood on his feet and said: Shot Mishot is located between the Tigris and Euphrates Rivers. The Gemara asks: And if it is located between the rivers, what of it? What halakha is this relevant for? Abaye said that Rabbi Ḥama bar Ukva says that Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says: The area between the rivers is like the exile, meaning Pumbedita, with regard to lineage. The Gemara inquires: And where is the area between the rivers located for the purpose of this halakha? Rabbi Yoḥanan said: From Ihi Dekira and upward, i.e., northward. The Gemara asks: But doesn’t Rabbi Yoḥanan say: Until the crossing at Gizma but no further? Abaye said: A strip extends from that region past Ihi Dekira.”

selectedQuotations.englishQuote: For Adam sinned through the seven species: wheat, barley, grape, fig, pomegranate, oil-bearing olive, and honey. Therefore the Sages of the Mishnah said that the tree from which Adam ate was wheat; others said that it was a vine, and others said that it was a fig tree. selectedQuotations.englishQuote: This is also alluded to in the verse, “So that you may recount in the ears of your son and your grandson.” It follows what I heard from the holy master, of blessed memory, who said that children are the depths of their father’s heart. Rabbi Menachem Azariah likewise wrote that the father’s soul is the son’s governing influence—that is, the root of life. This is the meaning of “So that you may recount”: through the locusts, they would attain the quality of understanding, the heart, and establish holiness for the generations—“So that you may recount.” In this He alluded to the plague of locusts, corresponding to understanding, the heart. Joel likewise says, “I will remove the northerner from you,” which in its plain meaning refers to the locusts. The Gemara, Sukkah 52a, says that Joel called it “the northerner,” and expounds: this is the evil inclination, which is hidden and stationed in a person’s heart. That is, in the hidden chambers of his heart. Thus the precise wording is “these signs of Mine within him.”

selectedQuotations.englishQuote: Although the Midrash, Rabbah and Tanchuma on Chukat, says, “His eye has seen every precious thing”—this refers to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues; matters not revealed to Moses were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues—and the Gemara there likewise says that Moses sat at the end of eight rows and did not understand what they were saying, nevertheless Rabbi Akiva did not apprehend the reason for a law given to Moses at Sinai, for that is Moses our teacher’s portion. Concerning this the Gemara says that Moses’s mind was put at ease: from this he saw that his understanding was higher, and that his portion of the Oral Torah was something no other person had attained. The portion of the Oral Torah belonging to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues does not pertain to Moses, because he had never brought about corruption and did not require the “abundant wisdom,” the fiftieth gate, entrusted to the penitent to repair the “abundant anger.”

selectedQuotations.englishQuote: According to Rabbi Eliezer, who holds that the world was created in Tishrei, the order is that redemption will be in Tishrei: on Rosh Hashanah there will be an awakening to repentance through the sounding of the shofar, as it says, “If a shofar is sounded in a city, will the people not tremble?” Afterward comes Yom Kippur, to repair all that has passed; when they merit it, the union will then take place. Afterward comes Sukkot, the season of our rejoicing, and the war of Gog and Magog on Sukkot. Although through repentance the time of redemption is always available—as it says, “Today, if you heed His voice,” as stated in Sanhedrin 98a—at its appointed time the awakening to repentance will come from God, as it says, “I will remove the heart of stone,” and “I will bring it about that you follow My statutes.” According to Rabbi Yehoshua, who holds that the world was created in Nisan, the spirit of the Messiah was then created so that redemption would take place in Nisan when its appointed time arrived. Its order will resemble the redemption from Egypt, initiated by God: there will be plagues, Israel will be refined in all ten attributes, and redemption will come from God.

selectedQuotations.hebrewQuote: ומצד השי"ת הסדר בחינת אברהם ואח"כ בחינת יצחק. דאברהם ששורש מדתו האהבה כמש"נ אברהם אוהבי ומצד האהבה בא הזריזות במ"ע. ויצחק שמדתו פחד יצחק היראה ומצדה בא הזהירות במצות ל"ת וכמו שאמרנו מהירושלמי (ונת' פ' חיי מאמר ז) והסדר מצד השי"ת אנכי ואח"כ לא יהיה שהשי"ת משפיע קדושה וד"ת ללב חכם לימינו ועי"ז נעקר הרע מלב כסיל לשמאלו וכמ"ש (שהש"ר פ' ישקני) שבשעה ששמעו דיבור אנכי נתקע ת"ת בלבם ובשעה ששמעו דיבור לא יהיה נעקר יצה"ר מלבם. דאנכי שורש כל המ"ע והד"ת. ולא יהיה שורש המצות ל"ת. ולכן מצד השי"ת הסדר נפש אברהם ואח"כ יצחק וכן יצאה ב"ק הלכה כב"ה שהם דרגא דאברהם. אבל מצד האדם הסדר סור מרע ואח"כ ועשה טוב. שלזכות לד"ת צריך שיוקדם היראה להיות סור מרע שהוא מדת יצחק אע"ה. וכן הוזכרו תמיד ב"ש קודם לב"ה.
selectedQuotations.englishQuote: From God’s side, the order is the quality of Abraham and afterward the quality of Isaac. The root of Abraham’s quality is love, as it says, “Abraham, who loved Me”; love brings eagerness in fulfilling positive commandments. Isaac’s quality, “the fear of Isaac,” is awe, which brings care in observing prohibitions, as we have explained from the Jerusalem Talmud, in Chayei Sarah, teaching 7. From God’s side, the order is “I am” and afterward “You shall have no other”: God bestows holiness and Torah upon “the wise person’s heart at his right,” and through this evil is uprooted from “the fool’s heart at his left.” As Shir HaShirim Rabbah, on “Let him kiss me,” states: when they heard the utterance “I am,” Torah study became fixed in their hearts; when they heard “You shall have no other,” the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts. “I am” is the root of all positive commandments and Torah teachings, while “You shall have no other” is the root of the prohibitions. Thus, from God’s side, Abraham’s soul comes first and afterward Isaac’s; likewise, a heavenly voice proclaimed that the halakhah follows Beit Hillel, who belong to Abraham’s level. From the human side, however, the order is “Turn from evil” and afterward “Do good.” To attain Torah, awe must come first, enabling one to turn from evil; this is the quality of our father Isaac, peace be upon him. Thus Beit Shammai are always mentioned before Beit Hillel.

selectedQuotations.englishQuote: On Shabbat, a Jew attains these three forms of humility. “Poor” corresponds to “From where did you come? From a putrid drop”: he is poor at his root. “Contrite of spirit”: when he takes to heart “Where are you going? To a place of dust,” his heart breaks within him and he becomes contrite of spirit. When he takes to heart that he will render an account before the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, he becomes one who “trembles at My word.” For who can stand before His judgment, and who can be innocent before Him? He becomes utterly humble in his own eyes, is saved from all three kinds of husks, and can merit complete redemption.

Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi heard what he had done and became angry with him. When Rabbi Ḥiyya came at some later date to visit him, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi mockingly said to him: Iyya, who is calling you outside? By asking this question Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi was intimating that Rabbi Ḥiyya should leave his house. sameSourceCatalog.targetEnglish: Abraham our father, being a father who included all the souls and needed to illuminate the entire world, was a vessel able to bear even this burning and blaze. God then illuminated for him through the lamp of particular commands, and his kidneys became fountains of wisdom; his descendants merited the lamp of the Sanctuary. The Sages said: God illuminates the entire world, yet commanded that light be given before Him. In truth, God is the One who gives the illumination that shines in the heart. Nevertheless He says that they should give light before Him: through what shines in Israel’s hearts, they illuminate before Him, so that He should not walk through dark passages. He describes it as their illuminating Him, rather than His illuminating them. This is the meaning of “He did not cease to cherish her until...,” and “Give strength to God.”

sameSourceCatalog.targetEnglish: At the close of Yom Kippur we likewise say seven times, “YHVH is God.” After Israel has repented and the gate of freedom—Binah, the world to come—has been revealed, this unity is mentioned seven times; seven is the number of completeness. This follows “Then you will understand ... and find knowledge of God”: one attains the inward knowledge through which this particular unity is attained, as in “Know today.” Every year Chanukah is a time when anyone can merit to repair his deeds so that they are reckoned as merits. If he opens one opening of repentance, like the point of a needle, through an awakening from his side, God is ready to help him attain the full repentance that turns deliberate sins into merits.

sameSourceCatalog.targetEnglish: This is through the first light, which was hidden for the righteous, the light called good. sameSourceCatalog.targetEnglish: All the nations heard, ‘Peoples tremble’: after seeing open, explicit miracles they could not deny them. Through this he becomes a scoffer and denies everything by mockery. This is ‘Amalek is the first of the nations,’ the beginning of the husk, for the root of the serpent’s enticement was ‘You will be like God.’ This is the utmost pride, as said concerning Nebuchadnezzar and Hiram, and it is the root of the evil inclination.

sameSourceCatalog.targetHebrew: וְהַיְנוּ דְּכָל הָאֻמּוֹת שָׁמְעוּ "עַמִּים יִרְגָּזוּן", מֵאַחַר שֶׁרָאוּ נִסִּים נִגְלִים וּמְפֹרָשִׁים וְלֹא יָכְלוּ לִכְפּוֹר, וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי לֵצָנוּת דָּחָה הַכֹּל וְכָפַר. וְזֶה בָּא מִגַּאֲוָה, שֶׁלֹּא יִתָּכֵן בְּעֵינָיו שֶׁיִּהְיֶה דָּבָר נֶעְלָם מִשִּׂכְלוֹ וְגָבוֹהַּ מֵהַשָּׂגָתוֹ, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשָׂה לֵץ וְכָפַר בַּכֹּל עַל יְדֵי לֵצָנוּת. וְהוּא "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם עֲמָלֵק", רֵאשִׁית דִּקְלִפָּה, דְּשֹׁרֶשׁ הַסָּתַת הַנָּחָשׁ הָיָה "וִהְיִיתֶם כֵּאלֹהִים", וְזֶה סוֹף הַגַּאֲוָה, וּכְמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בִּנְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר וּבְחִירָם, וְזֶהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע.
sameSourceCatalog.targetEnglish: All the nations heard, ‘Peoples tremble’: after seeing open, explicit miracles they could not deny them. But Amalek, through mockery, dismissed everything and denied it. This comes from pride: in his eyes it is impossible that anything should be hidden from his intellect and above his apprehension. Through this he becomes a scoffer and denies everything by mockery. This is ‘Amalek is the first of the nations,’ the beginning of the husk, for the root of the serpent’s enticement was ‘You will be like God.’ This is the utmost pride, as said concerning Nebuchadnezzar and Hiram, and it is the root of the evil inclination.

sameSourceCatalog.targetEnglish: Certainly the meaning is not that the wine caused the Egyptian exile as punishment. Rather, it resembles what they said in Nedarim: Why was Abraham our father punished, and his children enslaved in Egypt for two hundred and ten years? Because he pressed Torah scholars into service; because he overstepped concerning the Holy One’s attributes; or because he prevented people from entering beneath the wings of the Shekhinah. One must seemingly ask: what did Israel sin, that they should be enslaved for this? In truth the Egyptian exile was for Israel’s good, as preparation for receiving Torah. As stated in Berakhot: “The Holy One, blessed be He, gave Israel three good gifts, and gave them all only through afflictions: Torah,” and so forth. Through the afflictions of the Egyptian exile they merited Torah. The meaning of Abraham our father’s punishment is that he was informed of the Egyptian exile and the servitude, “They will serve them and afflict them.” The Talmud disputes the reason for this punishment.

sameSourceCatalog.targetHebrew: וְזֶה שֶׁהוֹדִיעוּהוּ בְּכָאן גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם, וּבַסּוֹף: "וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל", וְ"גָדוֹל" מוֹרֶה עַל מִדּוֹת עַתִּיקָא, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמְּקֻשָּׁרִין בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ, וְזֶה הָרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם, שֶׁנִּתְבָּרְרוּ שָׁם עַל יְדֵי הָעֶשֶׂר מַכּוֹת בְּכָל הָעֶשֶׂר מִדּוֹת, שֶׁבְּכָל מַכָּה יָצְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּדָּה אַחַת בַּקְּלִיפָּה, שֶׁיֵּשׁ גַּם כֵּן עֶשֶׂר זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה, וְנִכְנְסוּ בִּקְדוּשָׁה בְּמִדָּה אַחַת, עַד דֻּגְמַת מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, לו עַמּוּד א): "נָגוֹף לְמִצְרַיִם וְרָפוֹא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל".
sameSourceCatalog.targetEnglish: This is why he was informed here of the Egyptian exile and, at its end, “Afterward they will go out with great possessions.” “Great” indicates the qualities of Atika: being bound to the root. These are the great possessions they brought out of Egypt. Through the ten plagues they were clarified there in all ten qualities: in each plague Israel left one quality on the impure side, which also has ten corresponding qualities, and entered one quality in holiness. This resembles the holy Zohar’s expression, “Striking Egypt and healing Israel.”

sameSourceInherited.text: Moed Katan 16b: ‘Despite Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi’s decree, Rabbi Ḥiyya went out and taught his two nephews, Rav and Rabba bar bar Ḥana, in the marketplace. When Rabbi Ḥiyya came at some later date to visit him, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi mockingly said to him: Iyya, who is calling you outside? Because of unscrupulous women: if you say that it is not a valid bill of divorce, there may be a case in which he was prevented by circumstances beyond his control, but she says he was not; she goes and remarries, and the bill of divorce proves invalid and her children are mamzerim.

From a putrid drop”: he is poor at his root. “Contrite of spirit”: when he takes to heart “Where are you going? To a place of dust,” his heart breaks within him and he becomes contrite of spirit. When he takes to heart that he will render an account before the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, he becomes one who “trembles at My word.” For who can stand before His judgment, and who can be innocent before Him? He becomes utterly humble in his own eyes, is saved from all three kinds of husks, and can merit complete redemption.
